items.heading: B1. Neural specificity remains unestablished
items.exact_text:
### B1. Neural specificity remains unestablished

Validity, recursive qualification, the AVaR enclosure, the information lower bound, and the fallback are representation-neutral. The ReLU family is not the complete-work winner and is never certified adopted over quadratic least squares.
items.inherited_r119_author_treatment: The shared information theorem and original qualification remain representation-neutral. Exact ReLU/hinge identity now covers 96 paired files and 4,416 decisions. Fused qualification improves serving for multiple representations, but quadratic retains lower complete cost and original mean economic loss than ReLU. The separately frozen D validation adds independent original-primitive value bounds for all current delivered policies and retains all 56 arm comparisons. With the fixed left-minus-right arm ordering, the 56 contrasts comprise 32 strictly negative, 20 strictly positive, 2 exact-zero and 2 unresolved intervals. The two unresolved comparisons are quadratic versus the degree-two polynomial, one at each risk; the two exact zeros are ReLU versus the equivalent conventional hinge. The ReLU/ordinary-hinge equality and unchanged complete policies are explicit identities, so this validation supplies no architecture-exclusive economic gain.
items.inherited_r119_remaining_requirement: Neural-specific accuracy, information or adoption superiority is still not identified.
items.planned_r120_author_action: Every retained representation receives all four complete services: the completed incumbent, unchanged R108 legacy-safe policy changes, the new paired comparison using the same support-gradient proposal rules, and the stronger 512-node/24-bisection direct original-continuation proposal using the same paid pair certificate. The eight arms retain common access to the original formulas, feasible interval and certificate information. Each pays its actual standalone acquisition and complete service costs; the equivalent hinge pays the ReLU acquisition in full. Report own-incumbent gains separately from the cross-representation economic and resource frontier.
items.continuing_scientific_boundary: A benefit from a common original-risk correction is a contribution to the NBO decision mechanism. It is not a neural-exclusive representation advantage. Any stronger neural claim requires a separate equal-information and equal-resource separation.

items.heading: B2. The information-complexity result is too narrow for the platform claim
items.exact_text:
### B2. The information-complexity result is too narrow for the platform claim

The theorem is a specialized deterministic one-dimensional oracle result. It does not establish randomized, multivariate, nonuniform-law, or end-to-end Bellman complexity lower bounds.
items.inherited_r119_author_treatment: The information result is strengthened by an implementable paid-localization upper algorithm matching the lower order KR(1-alpha)/N^2 under one shared deterministic exact-point convention. The original investment certificate then carries the result into a real original-action calculation with finite-precision error paid.
items.inherited_r119_remaining_requirement: Randomized, nonuniform-law, multivariate and complete Bellman bit-complexity bounds remain outside the theorem, so broader platform complexity is not asserted.
items.planned_r120_author_action: The new original d=2 theorem proves a gradient modulus for the constrained AVaR continuation and an action-distance modulus for its difference. The fixed-known-tail information theorem gives matching interval-width order min(KR(1-alpha)/N^2, ER(1-alpha)/N) under one scalar-value-per-query convention. The original smooth continuation also gives the stronger separate-width coefficient 2*M_alpha*R^2*(1-alpha)^2; the generic lower adversary does not establish a lower bound for that stronger smooth or formula-informed class. The full original-policy certificate separately pays both risk deficits, actual point uncertainty and the unchanged future allowance. The finite-refinement proposition states the full positive gain margin and cap; it does not rebrand the achieved R119 tail-uniform theorem as new.
items.continuing_scientific_boundary: Optimal general randomized, nonuniform multivariate and complete learned Bellman complexity remain separate obligations unless actually proved. The scalar tail-uniform theorem does not pay for arbitrarily accurate floating-point values.
